subject: Proposal: capacity lock with variable rate windows — FinThrive hosted commit
messages:
From: Samantha Liu <samantha@finthrive.com>
To: dylan@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 02 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API capacity increase and rate flexibility

Hi Dylan,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team was impressed with the latency profile and the billing transparency. We kicked off a usage analysis and it looks like our Q3 projections will exceed our current hosted commit by ~3.5x (spike around campaign windows). Attached is our April usage export so you can see the shape.

We have three asks as we look at renewal and expansion:
- Lock a higher monthly committed volume for 12 months with predictable base rates.
- Allow 2 configurable burst windows per month (up to 2x commit) at defined premium rates.
- A 60-day review clause to adjust commit after the first two months if our forecasts materially change.

Can you put together a short proposal with pricing options (monthly commit levels, burst rates, and any early-termination / review language)? Procurement wants a clean path to sign within 2 weeks if we can agree on rates.

Attachment: finthrive-usage-report-apr2028.csv

Would appreciate a draft by next Wed.

Best,
Samantha Liu
Head of Platform Partnerships
FinThrive

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Liu <samantha@finthrive.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 02 May 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API capacity increase and rate flexibility

Hi Samantha — thanks for the data and for outlining the asks. This is exactly the kind of account we like to build longer-term partnerships with.

Quick confirmation: we can do a 12-month committed contract with explicit burst windows. I pulled an initial sketch and attached a one-page draft that covers two structured options (monthly commit bands + burst pricing).

Next steps I propose:
- I’ll put Karthik on pricing finalization and Marissa on ops/throughput guardrails.
- If you’re comfortable with one of the options we’ll issue a term sheet and a DocuSign routing for signatures.
- We can include the 60-day review clause you requested (standard language) and a one-time transition credit if you sign before month-end.

I’ve copied an internal link with detailed botched traffic curves so the pricing team can see tail latency assumptions: https://drive.google.com/rdw/proposal/finthrive-draft

Attachment: rdw-proposal-draft-v1.pdf

Thanks — will follow up before Wednesday with Karthik’s recommendation.

—Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 04 May 2028 08:20:00 -0700
Subject: Pricing options for FinThrive (draft)

Dylan / Marissa — draft pricing thoughts below based on the CSV and the projected 3.5x spike. I recommend we lead with Option B to strike a balance between unit economics and operational flexibility.

Option A — Conservative (lower commit, higher burst)
- Monthly commit: 4M tokens/month
- Base price: $0.00105 per token (billed against commit)
- Burst windows: 2x commit up to 8M tokens at $0.0016 per excess token
- Annual prepay discount: 5%
- Ops note: burst allowed but throttled after sustained 30min of >1.8x baseline

Option B — Recommended (higher commit, lower unit cost)
- Monthly commit: 12M tokens/month
- Base price: $0.00078 per token
- Burst windows: 2x commit up to 24M tokens at $0.0012 per excess token
- Annual prepay discount: 10% (or 7% for quarterly invoicing)
- Included: 2 reserved burst windows per month (30–120 min each), automatic fallback to smaller model variant if sustained >2x

Other commercial points:
- 60-day review clause: standard — either party may request a commit adjustment after 60 days with 30 days’ notice; adjustment triggers pro-rated billing reconciliation.
- SLA: 99.9% availability for hosted endpoints; white-glove support during initial 30-day ramp window.

Attachments to include in final: redwood-term-sheet-v3.pdf (term sheet with T&Cs), final pricing appendix.

I recommend we present Option B to FinThrive with a 10% incentive if they sign a 12-month annual prepay.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, Pricing & GTM Economics
Redwood Inference
From: Samantha Liu <samantha@finthrive.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
Cc: FinThrive Procurement <procurement@finthrive.com>
Date: Fri, 10 May 2028 15:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API capacity increase and rate flexibility

Thanks, Dylan — and please pass my thanks to Karthik and Marissa for the quick turnaround. Option B looks closest to what we need. A few clarifications before procurement will sign:

1) Can you confirm the effective per-token rate in the DocuSign term sheet after the 10% annual prepay incentive?
2) We need the two burst windows to be configurable on our side (start/end times) with a 2-hour minimum and the ability to move one window per month with 48-hour notice.
3) We’d like a 60-day review clause that allows either party to propose a +/- commit adjustment; any increase should be back-dated to when usage exceeded the commit.

If you can reflect the answers in the final term sheet and route via DocuSign we can get signatures within 48 hours. Otherwise we’ll need to push to next week.

Attachment: redwood-term-sheet-v3.pdf

Looking forward to the DocuSign link.

Best,
Samantha
Head of Platform Partnerships, FinThrive
